# #448 — The policy layer is in no index — agents cannot find the rules they are judged by

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: wayfinder:task
Created: 2026-07-29T19:21:33Z
Updated: 2026-07-29T19:21:33Z

---

## Question

How do agents reach a procedure that already exists?

The policy layer — Development-wide `_DOCS/` and `_ob/` — is in **no search
index**. Measured 2026-07-29: the fleet index holds 10,900 documents across 40+
repo collections and **zero** from either tree.

Consequences, both observed in one session:

- `_DOCS/QMD_INDEXES.md` is complete (150 lines, the general form, the naming
  standard, a worked example). An `ai-agents` session could not find it,
  improvised, ran `qmd-backfill` on a third-party checkout, and committed an
  index allowlist into `github.com/block/buzz`.
- `_ob/skills/skill-maintainer/workflows/update.md` says editing a runtime
  adapter instead of the canonical is a fork. Unreachable by search; this session
  did exactly that.

The rules that govern how every agent works are the only knowledge not
searchable, so agents reliably fail in the ways those rules warn about.

Scope: a named `policy` index over `_DOCS` + `_ob` using the existing
parameterized builder (`ROOT=... INDEX=policy qmd-reference-index`), and routing
so ordinary agent searches reach it. `aqmd` scopes to the current repo by design
— that guard exists because unscoped runs cost a GPU hour — so widening the repo
index is the wrong fix.

**Retrieval half only.** Canon (#444) carries the one-line rule; this serves the
full text on trigger. Index-only is what already failed: an agent that does not
know a rule exists never searches for it.

Type: task (AFK).
